entries.title: AMD Am386DX
entries.description: 32-bit x86 · 32-bit external data bus
entries.dateNote: AMD’s annual report explicitly dates the Am386 family introduction to 1991. This is the 32-bit external-bus DX profile; the pictured 40 MHz grade is not claimed to date every package or revision.

image.caption: Motherboard with an AMD Am386DX-40; this later speed grade illustrates the 1991 family.

entries.summary: AMD's 32-bit 386DX CPU

entries.title: AMD Am386SX
entries.description: 32-bit x86 · 16-bit external data bus
entries.dateNote: AMD’s Am386SX Rev A sheet is dated March 1991. The SX has a 16-bit external data bus; later SXL/SXLV power and speed variants require separate dates and contracts.

image.caption: AMD Am386SX/SXL-25 package; the pictured later SXL variant illustrates the SX family.

entries.summary: AMD's 386 CPU with a 16-bit bus

entries.title: IBM 386SLC
entries.description: 386SX-derived IBM CPU · 8 KB internal cache
entries.dateNote: IBM announcement 191-201, October 17, 1991, specifies the 20 MHz 386SLC and 8 KB internal cache, with December availability planned. The Model 56 SLC followed in 1992; this is not Intel 386SL or a 486SLC.

image.alt: IBM PS/2 family hosts; the individual 386SLC processor is not pictured.
image.caption: IBM PS/2 family hosts; the individual 386SLC processor is not pictured.

entries.summary: IBM's 386-class CPU with an 8 KB on-chip cache

entries.title: IBM PS/2 Model 35 SX
entries.description: 20 MHz 386SX · 16-bit ISA · VGA & IDE
entries.dateNote: IBM announcement 191-075 gives June 11, 1991 availability and a 20 MHz 80386SX. Model 35 SX uses ISA; the later 35 SLC is a separate profile. The photograph is a representative PS/2 family view.

image.alt: Representative PS/2 family: PS/2E above Model 56 and Model 30-286; not a Model 35 SX.
image.caption: Representative PS/2 family: PS/2E above Model 56 and Model 30-286; not a Model 35 SX.

entries.title: IBM PS/2 Model 25 SX
entries.description: 16 MHz 386SX · 16-bit ISA · integrated color VGA
entries.dateNote: IBM letter 192-019 (January 21, 1992) specifies a 16 MHz 80386SX, with April 17 planned availability. The selected K00 profile replaces the Compaq 386s SX build; the photograph is a representative Model 25 chassis, not a confirmed K00 planar.

image.alt: IBM Model 25 family chassis; the selected 1992 SX board revision is not confirmed in this photo.
image.caption: IBM Model 25 family chassis; the selected 1992 SX board revision is not confirmed in this photo.

entries.summary: IBM PS/2 Model 25 desktop with a 16 MHz 386SX

entries.title: IBM PS/2 Model 56 SLC
entries.description: 20 MHz IBM 386SLC · 16-bit Micro Channel · SCSI
entries.dateNote: IBM’s preserved specification gives February 25, 1992: 20 MHz IBM 386SLC, 8 KB cache, 16-bit Micro Channel and integrated SCSI. The selected 8556-055 is distinct from plain SX, LS and later SLC2 variants; the pictured Model 56 revision is unconfirmed.

image.alt: IBM PS/2E above a Model 56 and Model 30-286; the Model 56 SLC planar revision is unconfirmed.
image.caption: IBM PS/2E above a Model 56 and Model 30-286; the Model 56 SLC planar revision is unconfirmed.
